market.mood: Risk-off and jittery: the S&P 500 closed Tuesday at its lowest level since late July and the Nasdaq touched a seven-month low as AI and chip stocks sold off, then steadied Wednesday after Nvidia cleared its earnings bar.

themes.title: Fed is on track to hike in December; 10-year yield above 5%
themes.what_happened: October CPI rose 0.4% m/m, hotter than forecast, and core rose 0.3% for the third straight month. The 10-year yield is about 5.11%, St. Louis Fed's Musalem says as many as four more hikes may be needed, and CME pricing shows a 95% chance of a 25bp hike in December.
themes.why_it_matters: A tightening cycle with 5% long yields compresses multiples on long-duration growth and AI names and pressures rate-sensitive sectors like utilities.

our_exposure.why: Utilities fell 1.6% Tuesday; high yields pressure the sector's valuation.
Long-duration AI growth multiples are sensitive to 5% yields.
High-beta tech leaders are vulnerable to further rate repricing.

Financials lagged most (-1.9%) Tuesday, though higher rates can support margins.

themes.next: FOMC October minutes due Wednesday; Fed meeting Dec 8-9 (Waller has floated 50bp if core inflation stays hot); next CPI is the last data point before then.

themes.title: AI trade wobbles: Nvidia sell-off, Huang exit, then an earnings beat
themes.what_happened: Jensen Huang resigned as CEO last Thursday, and Nvidia shares lost nearly 15% over the past week and nearly 30% over the past month. Q3 revenue was $115.84B versus about $109B expected, with Q4 guidance of $130B versus $125.1B consensus. The chair said Huang would not return as CEO. Nvidia rose early Wednesday but trimmed gains, and neoclouds CoreWeave, Iren and Nebius fell.
themes.why_it_matters: Nvidia is a roughly $3.75T bellwether, so its results and leadership uncertainty set direction for the whole AI hardware chain.

our_exposure.why: Strong guide, but CEO vacuum and a fading post-earnings bounce.
AI-server demand confirmed by guidance; sentiment still fragile.
AI server demand supported; sector sentiment fragile.
Data-center power and cooling demand tied to Nvidia guidance.
AI memory demand supported; chip sentiment volatile.
AI storage and memory demand supported; chip sentiment volatile.

AI power-demand thesis supported, but AI-sentiment swings hit the stock.

themes.next: Kulicke & Soffa reports after Wednesday's close, a read on whether AI demand reaches equipment suppliers. Watch whether Nvidia holds its post-earnings gains and any news on a permanent CEO.

themes.title: Anthropic IPO: a roughly $64B test of AI risk appetite
themes.what_happened: Anthropic prices tonight: 825M shares at $70-$78, about $64.35B raised at the top, trading on Nasdaq Thursday. The WSJ reports it could price above $80. AMD, Broadcom, Google, Micron, Microsoft, Nvidia and TSMC Partners agreed to buy $26B of shares in a private placement, with Google and Nvidia each committing $10B.
themes.why_it_matters: A huge supply of AI equity could drain liquidity from other AI names if it trades poorly, while a strong debut would validate AI valuations.

our_exposure.why: Committed $10B to the IPO placement; strong debut marks up its stake.
Committed $10B to the placement; strong debut validates AI demand.
Placement participant; strong debut supports AI memory demand.
Robinhood is among brokers selling IPO shares; retail flows help.
Earlier reporting says Amazon backs Anthropic; competes with it in cloud.

themes.next: Final price Wednesday evening ET; first trade Thursday Nov 19. Watch whether pricing exceeds the $70-$78 range and how the open affects the Nasdaq and AI complex.

themes.title: US-Iran war escalates, but oil is falling on returning supply
themes.what_happened: US-Iran strikes resumed in recent days, and Iran says Hormuz stays shut until its conditions are met. Even so, Brent and WTI are on track for declines of about 20% this month. Brent is around $93 and WTI about $85.5. Hormuz flows jumped 78% in Q3, and the IEA forecasts a roughly 2 million-barrel-a-day surplus.
themes.why_it_matters: Falling crude eases the inflation worry behind the Fed hikes, but a flare-up in the Gulf could send oil sharply higher again.

our_exposure.why: Lower crude pressures upstream earnings; Energy held up best Tuesday.
Lower crude pressures upstream earnings; small position.
Cheaper fuel eases pressure on consumers; modest indirect benefit.
Lower oil reduces input and freight costs.
Lower oil reduces input and freight costs.

themes.next: Weekly EIA inventory data; Qatar-mediated talks and any Hormuz shipping incidents. Oil has swung on weekend escalation fears and early-week reversals.
